It’s been a little over a year and a half now that things have felt…wrong. At first I just thought it was stress from the call center, the constant angry customers, the divorce. But then I became convinced something bigger was happening. I can’t shake this feeling that everything is collapsing, like the world is winding down and some huge disaster is already set in motion. It doesn’t feel like a worry; it feels like a fact.

I used to unwind with gaming, podcasts, going out with my team after shifts. Now none of that does anything for me. It’s like my brain can’t register enjoyment. Most days I feel hollow, like I’m watching my own life on mute. Sometimes my emotions feel so far away that I just sort of shut down and sit there, not moving, not answering people.

Other times I’m the opposite—pacing around my apartment, picking at my fingers, unable to sit through a Zoom meeting. Sleep is awful. I wake up from these vivid, terrifying dreams several times a week, soaked in sweat. And occasionally I get this strange taste in my mouth—metallic or rotten—when I’m not eating anything. It makes me wonder if it’s another sign that something terrible is coming. My work performance has definitely taken a hit; I’m falling behind on tickets and losing track of conversations with my team.

Most days I’m either pacing around my apartment, wringing my hands, or picking at my skin, unable to sit still, or I’m just sitting there staring, not really moving or responding to anything. My ex says I sometimes “shut down” completely for long stretches.

The whole time, I’ve been convinced something terrible is coming, like the world is about to collapse or already has and we just haven’t noticed yet. That idea doesn’t really go away, even when my mood is more neutral. Sometimes I taste this awful chemical, metallic flavor out of nowhere, like poison in my mouth, when I’m alone.

Sleep is awful. For more than a year I’ve had these intense nightmares almost every night—catastrophes, the world ending. I wake up drenched in sweat and then drag myself through work on autopilot. It’s been going on most of the time since this all started.
D007-D005_h025.question_b:
It’s been about a year and seven months since things really went off the rails. I keep having this fixed feeling that something terrible is coming, like the world is winding down. It doesn’t feel like a fear; it feels like a fact, like everything around me is hollow and about to collapse. Sometimes even water or coffee tastes wrong—metallic, like poison—when I know it shouldn’t, but I can’t shake the sense that something’s tainted.

At work, when people ask me simple questions, my answers wander. I’ll start explaining a ticket, then I’m talking about the servers, then about the power grid, then about how it won’t matter when everything shuts down. I can see people getting confused, but pulling myself back to the point is really hard.

Most days I just don’t care about anything I used to enjoy—movies, games, even seeing my kids on weekends feels flat. For the last year and a half or so, there’ve been stretches where I feel emotionally shut off, like I’m watching my own life from outside. During those times I pace a lot, pick at my fingers, can’t sit still, and my sleep is wrecked by these vivid nightmares about cities burning or skies going black. Those “down” periods come and go, but the weird beliefs and the emptiness have been there the whole time.

Sometimes, when it gets really bad, I just freeze up. My ex found me once sitting on the couch for over an hour, barely moving, staring at the wall, not responding to her or to my phone ringing. It was like I couldn’t make my body or my mouth do anything, even though I was vaguely aware people were around me.
